name: Low-Dose Carboplatin + Etoposide (Low-Risk / Symptomatic Infant Neuroblastoma)

source.textbook: Principles and Practice of Pediatric Oncology, 8th ed.

institution.provenance: COG Low-Risk Neuroblastoma Protocol (Strother et al. J Clin Oncol 2012)

histology: neuroblastoma (low-risk, favorable biology, symptomatic organ compromise)
supportiveCare: Hydration with D5 0.45% NS at maintenance rate during chemotherapy
Careful fluid and electrolyte balance in infants with massive hepatomegaly (stage MS/4S)
monitoring: Electrolytes, BUN, creatinine prior to each cycle
Serial abdominal ultrasound and urine HVA/VMA to evaluate organ decompression

drugs.name: Carboplatin
drugs.notes: Carboplatin 187 mg/m2 IV over 1 hour on Day 1 (or 6.2 mg/kg in infants <12 kg). Indicated strictly for symptomatic life- or organ-threatening complications.

drugs.name: Etoposide
drugs.notes: Etoposide 100 mg/m2/day IV over 2 hours on Days 1-3 (or 3.3 mg/kg/day in infants <12 kg).
